use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: C2 JU resolves dual designations by correlating two ballistic missile tracks reported on the interface that are eligible for correlation, so that each track represents a single data point.

scope_contract.goal_statement: C2 JU resolves dual designations by correlating two ballistic missile tracks reported on the interface that are eligible for correlation, so that each track represents a single data point.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Two ballistic missile tracks are reported on the interface and are eligible for correlation; C2 JU correlates them, thereby resolving the dual designation so that the interface reports a single data point.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Two ballistic missile tracks are reported on the interface and are eligible for correlation.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The dual designation is resolved; the correlated track represents a single data point on the interface.
in_scope_actions: Correlate two eligible ballistic missile tracks reported on the interface
Resolve the dual designation through that correlation
excluded_adjacent_actions: Using PPLI data to reduce surveillance-track reporting redundancy
General protocol-level minimization of occurrence/duration of dual designations outside the correlation action
variant_dimensions: No selectable categories are specified in the cited goal evidence

claims.content: C2 JU
Two tracks are reported on the interface and are recognized by the C2 JU as candidates for correlation.
The positions of all tracks and IUs tested for correlation are extrapolated to the same time.

Upon receipt of a remote real-time J3.2 or J3.3 track (or J2.0/J2.2/J2.3 PPLI report) not confirmed to have an existing correlation, or immediately prior to each transmission of a local track, the C2 JU initiates an automatic correlation test.
The C2 JU continuously correlates locally derived ballistic missile tracks with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG.

The C2 JU automatically performs a correlation test upon receipt of a remote real-time J3.2 or J3.3 track (or J2.0/J2.2/J2.3 PPLI report) not confirmed to have an existing correlation, or immediately prior to each transmission of a local track.
The correlation process compares locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, altitude, and boost indication) with the data received on the interface.
When the two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, they are deemed a tentative correlation.
The same two tracks are tested again upon the next correlation stimulus; two tracks shall pass the correlation tests and restrictions before the correlation is executed.

When the two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction, they are processed for dual designation resolution in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1j and k.

The C2 JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks, with the Retained TN/Dropped TN selection made in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.1j; the message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.

The receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
After the J7.2 message, the C2 JU holding R2 for the Dropped TN drops the Dropped TN, ceases reporting that track, and transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.

Diverges from Step 2: The C2 JU may manually initiate correlation of any two tracks, without applying the correlation test criteria, correlation restrictions, or correlation requirements, except that manual correlation is not permitted when the tracks are of a different E/C, one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote.

Diverges from Step 6: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator is alerted to take one of the following actions: change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation, or transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.

Diverges from Step 6: Automatic correlation may be allowed despite conflicting IDs when either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation and has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend.

Diverges from Step 6: If the Identity or Identity Amplifying Descriptor (IAD) of the Retained TN and the Dropped TN are different and the difference would result in automatic acceptance of the Dropped TN ID/IAD, the Dropped TN ID/IAD and Special Interest Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type shall be transferred to the Retained TN.
Diverges from Step 6: When the Identity of the Retained TN and the Dropped TN are the same, associated identification data reported for the Retained TN shall be retained.
Diverges from Step 8: A C2 JU responding with a reverse correlation shall transmit the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.

Diverges from Step 8: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held, the Dropped TN has an OCC, and RV is set to 3, the system shall execute the correlation using the Dropped TN data and the Retained TN track number.
Diverges from Step 9: When a J7.2 message is initiated by own unit and a Drop Track message has not yet been received for the Dropped TN, the Dropped TN shall be retained as a remote track.

Diverges from Step 6: If a ballistic missile track being processed for dual-designation resolution is lost (the reporting JU with R² has received no local sensor data since the last transmitted update, or has determined the track is lost by other system criteria), the track is reported with held data and Lost Track Indicator set to 1; a JU reporting such a Lost Track is assumed to have a TQ 5 less than the value being reported (for example, Lost Track TQ 15 permits a JU holding Tracking data to assume R² with TQ 11).

Diverges from Step 8: If prespecified conditions exist that require or allow rejection of the requested correlation — including the receiving IU holding OCCs on both tracks, or holding conflicting IDs on the two tracks while the ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled — the receiving IU rejects the correlation; whenever a correlation request is rejected, a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 is transmitted to report the rejection. Exit: the requested correlation is rejected and the rejection is reported.

Diverges from Step 9: When it is determined that more than one data point exists for a ballistic missile track currently being reported, track decorrelation should occur. If the Retained TN and Dropped TN decorrelate when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once, the correlation shall be rejected. Exit: the correlation is rejected.
The dual designation is resolved via correlation; the correlated ballistic missile track represents a single data point on the interface.

Upon acceptance of the requested correlation, the receiving IUs retain the designated Retained TN and drop the designated Dropped TN; if the originating C2 JU holds R2 for the Dropped TN, it drops the Dropped TN and transmits the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

Upon correlation execution, the Dropped TN's Latitude, Longitude, Course, Speed, Altitude, Altitude Source, TQ, and Strength (if the Dropped TN was a local or common local track) are transferred to the Retained TN.

Identification and IFF/SIF data are applied to the Retained TN per the correlation rules: if ID conflict restrictions apply and IDs differ, the last Identity reported for the Dropped TN is processed as an Identity Difference Report for the Retained TN; otherwise, the applicable ID/IAD and platform attributes are transferred; any nonzero Mode I/II/III IFF/SIF data from the Dropped TN is transferred when the corresponding Retained TN data is zero.
After acceptance of a manual correlation (RV field set to value 3), the resulting track is not subject to automatic decorrelation processing for 5 minutes.

quality_flags.detail: [exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 1 describes lost-track reporting and the adjusted R²/TQ assumption, but does not state what happens to the dual-designation/correlation process after the track is lost. There is no return to a Main Flow step, termination/hand-off, or explicit terminal state. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit recovery/exit behavior is not supported by the cited evidence; e.g., that the JU holding Tracking data assumes R² with TQ 11 as the resulting state of the lost-track exception branch.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 3 states that track decorrelation should occur when more than one data point exists, but it does not describe the resulting state or completion of decorrelation. No return to Main Flow, termination/hand-off, or explicit terminal state is provided. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit exit/termination behavior after the rejection is reported is not supported by the cited evidence.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 0 describes the lost-track reporting and the adjusted TQ assumption, but does not state an exit, return, hand-off, or terminal failure/prevention state for the use case. It is unclear whether the dual-designation resolution is aborted, deferred, or resumes at a main-flow step after the lost-track report. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit recovery/exit evidence for the exception branch after the tracking JU assumes R², including how lost-track handling completes.; Evidence that the track is reported with held data.))

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] The main flow is an automatic correlation test from trigger through step 6, with no manual correlation action or RV=3 branch. Postcondition 5 guarantees behavior only after acceptance of a manual correlation, so it is not reachable from the main flow.

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] Trigger includes J2.0/J2.2/J2.3 PPLI reports as events that initiate the automatic correlation test, but the main flow only describes correlation of ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG and never defines the PPLI-report processing path. Thus the PPLI-triggered scenario does not continue into the main flow.

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception Flow claim 1 (Diverges from Step 6) describes reporting a lost track with held data and Lost Track Indicator set to 1, but it never states how the branch ends: it does not return to a Main Flow step, terminate/hand off, or reach an explicit terminal failure/prevention state (e.g., correlation not executed/aborted). The branch outcome is therefore ambiguous.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger says the C2 JU recognizes two tracks as already eligible and then initiates action, but the Main Flow steps 1-5 restart at the correlation-testing process that produces that eligibility (continuous correlation, first-pass tentative, second-pass confirmation). This is a vertical-flow restart rather than a continuation from the Trigger. Preconditions also assert eligibility is already satisfied, making the Main Flow test steps appear to occur before the use case begins. The concrete triggering stimulus in the Main Flow is step 2: receipt of an uncorrelated remote track/PPLI or imminent local transmission.

Preconditions assert that the two tracks have already satisfied the correlation eligibility tests and restrictions before the use case begins. The Trigger, however, is the initiation of an automatic correlation test, and Main Flow steps 4–5 still require a first tentative pass and a second pass before correlation is executed. The precondition therefore assumes the outcome of the Main Flow's own test steps, making the Trigger/main flow unreachable from the stated starting state.

Exception flow claim 2 says 'track decorrelation should occur' when more than one data point exists, but it does not specify a clear outcome: no return to a main-flow step, no termination/hand-off, and no explicit terminal failure/prevention state is stated.

The last postcondition is about acceptance of a manual correlation (RV field set to value 3) and the resulting 5-minute decorrelation stability. The Trigger and Main Flow describe only automatic correlation testing and automatic J7.2 transmission, so no action in the Main Flow leads to this manual-correlation postcondition.
